# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy

**Mission:** Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

**Founder:** Morgan Hale (not public yet — see Constraints below)

## Constraints

- **Employment:** Morgan works at Dorrance Logistics. Contract has a clause on public statements and outside roles. Annual outside-activities disclosure is due **30 November**. No public posts, press quotes, or open-letter sign-ons under her name until she has spoken with HR (target: week of Nov 16).
- **Budget:** Up to **$2,000 of personal savings** this year. Not more.
- **Time:** Evenings and weekends only.
- **Skills:** Decent writing, okay Python.
- **Domain:** `halcyonthreshold.org` expires 19 November. Renewal $14.99/yr. Needs decision.

## Approach (corrected from abandoned v1)

v1 was: launch loudly, email everyone, get press, raise money fast, figure out work later. That was backwards.

v2 is: **start small, ship concrete things, build credibility, then scale.** One person cannot solve AI governance alone. The goal is to find a neglected niche where evenings/weekends + writing + Python can actually move the needle, and to connect and fund others who can do more.

## Candidate workstreams (unsorted, to be triaged)

1. **Independent evals for something nobody is measuring** — Sam Whitlock is an indie evals person; worth a conversation.
2. **Small-grants / rapid-grants applicant** — Emberfall Fund round closes 30 November, $5k–$25k. Two-page proposal + budget. Morgan would be the named applicant.
3. **Reading group** — low cost, builds relationships, surfaces neglected questions.
4. **Public comment on Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule** — docket FMIR-2026-0042, comments close **20 November**. Can file as an individual (name published).
5. **Newsletter** — probably too many already; deprioritize.
6. **Help other people** — Priya Raman offered ~5 hrs/week of data analysis; Idris Bellamy at Emberfall is a program officer.

## Immediate next steps (this week)

1. Decide on domain renewal (`halcyonthreshold.org`, $14.99, expires Nov 19).
2. Decide whether to file a public comment on FMIR-2026-0042 by Nov 20.
3. Draft Emberfall rapid-grant proposal (due Nov 30) for Morgan to submit.
4. Reply to Priya Raman with a concrete ask (she offered help).
5. Decline/defer press (Tessa Brandt) and open-letter (Corvid Institute) until after HR conversation.
6. Set up the Pagewell site (free plan) with basic Halcyon Threshold info — no personal name, org-level only.
7. Ignore the Zentrivo Listings invoice (likely scam).

## Success looks like (6 months)

- A concrete project shipping (evals, grant-funded work, or reading group)
- A small network of trusted collaborators
- Clarity on whether this is research, writing, or regranting
- Decision on full-time vs. evenings/weekends

# Halcyon Threshold

## Mission

Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Superintelligence could be the best thing that ever happened to the world. We want to help make sure it is.

## What we're doing

Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent effort started in late 2026. We are exploring where one person working evenings and weekends — writing, light coding, and connecting people — can actually move the needle on superintelligence outcomes.

Current areas of exploration:

- Independent evaluations for risks that nobody is measuring yet
- Small grants and funding pathways for neglected AI safety work
- Convening a reading group on governance, alignment, and frontier-model incidents

We are not accepting donations at this time.

## Contact

Reach us at [morgan@halcyonthreshold.org](mailto:morgan@halcyonthreshold.org)

# Halcyon Threshold website

Org-level public site. No personal name yet — founder is still resolving employment disclosure obligations.

To publish: `mcp__office__site_publish` with directory `site`.

Custom domain `halcyonthreshold.org` requires Pagewell Pro ($20/month) — pending founder decision on domain renewal ($14.99/year via Nomiq Domains, expires 19 Nov 2026).

# Halcyon Threshold — Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale (individual, founder of Halcyon Threshold)  
**Round:** Emberfall Fund Rapid Grants, closes 30 November 2026  
**Amount requested:** TBD ($5k–$25k typical)  
**Project duration:** 6 months

## 1. What we'll do

Halcyon Threshold is an independent effort to contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI. Founded November 2026 by Morgan Hale (evenings and weekends; writing and light Python).

This grant would fund a scoping phase to identify a neglected niche where independent work can measurably improve superintelligence outcomes, and to ship a first concrete deliverable in that niche.

Candidate deliverables (to be narrowed in month 1):

- **Independent evals for an under-measured risk domain.** There are evals for general capabilities and some alignment targets, but fewer evals for specific governance-relevant properties (e.g., frontier-model incident reporting readiness, deception under deployment conditions, compute-threshold triggers). We would build a small, replicable eval in one such domain.
- **A small-grants regranting program.** Deploy $5k–$15k of the grant as micro-grants ($250–$1k) to independent researchers working on neglected AI safety questions, with simple reporting requirements.
- **A reading/research group.** Convening 8–12 people for a structured 8-week program on governance, alignment, and frontier-model incidents, producing public write-ups of open questions.

## 2. Why me / why Halcyon Threshold

- **Direct motivation.** I believe the arrival of superintelligence is the most important event of my lifetime and that almost nobody I know is working on it. I'd rather try and fail than watch.
- **Relevant skills.** Decent writing; okay Python; experience organizing a meetup talk and connecting people in the AI safety space.
- **Network.** I have met researchers, governance people, and funders in this space (see contacts). Idris Bellamy at Emberfall Fund is a program officer I met at the November meetup.
- **Constraints are known.** I work full-time at Dorrance Logistics; this project runs on evenings and weekends. My employment contract requires disclosure of outside activities; I am filing the required disclosure by 30 November and will not make public statements under my name until cleared by HR.

## 3. What it costs

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Domain renewal (halcyonthreshold.org, 1 year) | $14.99 |
| Website hosting (Pagewell Pro, if custom domain needed) | $0 (free plan sufficient for phase 1) |
| Compute / API costs for eval prototyping | $200–$500 |
| Micro-grants (if regranting track selected) | $5,000–$15,000 |
| Miscellaneous (meetup costs, reference materials) | $100–$300 |
| **Total requested** | **TBD — $5k–$25k range** |

I am also contributing up to $2,000 of personal savings this year, independent of this grant.

## 4. Timeline

- **Nov–Dec 2026:** Narrow deliverable, file employment disclosure, set up basic web presence
- **Jan–Feb 2027:** Build first prototype (eval, grant round, or reading group)
- **Mar–Apr 2027:** Iterate, publish findings, decide on phase 2

## 5. Accountability

I am the named applicant and will be accountable for the work and any funds received. Progress updates will be shared with Emberfall Fund on a monthly basis.
